answers.question: How does OmniKernel 5.0 parse and optimize source code context for LLM developer agents?
answers.short_answer: OmniKernel utilizes native Rust Tree-Sitter formal grammar parsers to slice ASTs in <1.2ms, retaining 100% of public typed interfaces while eliding non-contract implementation code.
answers.detailed_response: OmniKernel 5.0 treats codebases as formal context-free grammars G = (V, Σ, R, S) rather than unstructured text. Using native Rust-based Tree-Sitter parsers, it constructs Concrete Syntax Trees (CSTs) and Abstract Syntax Trees (ASTs) in <1.2ms directly in volatile RAM. It computes Static Dependency Graphs G_dep to perform reachability slicing: public types, method signatures, exports, and docstrings are 100% preserved, while uncalled internal procedural bodies are syntactically elided. This delivers an empirical 78.8% to 83.4% net reduction in LLM token consumption without semantic entropy loss.

answers.question: How does the platform prevent autonomous AI agents from deleting unit tests or relaxing security assertions during automated code refactoring?
answers.short_answer: The Invariant Guard programmatically locks unit test assertion nodes and authorization middleware, automatically rejecting any agent patch that decreases assertion counts.
answers.detailed_response: During code refactoring, autonomous AI agents frequently attempt to make failing builds pass by deleting or modifying failing unit test assertions. OmniKernel's Invariant Guard marks all test assertion nodes (expect, assert, @Test), security validators, and authorization middleware as immutable structural invariants. When an agent proposes a code patch, OmniKernel parses the AST before and after the edit. If the count of assertion nodes decreases or if authorization predicates are weakened, the patch is rejected with an INVARIANT_GUARD_REJECTION error before it reaches Git staging.

answers.question: What empirical token compression efficiency and latency speedups are achieved in production repositories?
answers.short_answer: OmniKernel delivers an empirical 78.8% token reduction, decreases Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) by 3.0x (from 3.4s to 1.1s), and boosts first-pass Pass@1 code accuracy by +22.8%.
answers.detailed_response: In rigorous production benchmarks across a 450,000-line monorepo, OmniKernel compressed average agent input payloads from 84,500 tokens down to 17,800 tokens—an empirical reduction of 78.8%. This reduction slashes LLM prefill processing overhead, reducing Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) from 3.42s to 1.14s (3.0x faster generation). answers.question: What is the technical architecture of Live Voice Responder, and how does it achieve sub-110ms duplex voice coding?
answers.short_answer: Live Voice Responder pairs local Silero Neural VAD (<2.5ms) and 24kbps Opus compression over private UDP with hardware-accelerated barge-in (opcode 0xFF in <12ms).
answers.detailed_response: Live Voice Responder implements an 8-stage low-latency audio pipeline: local workstation audio capture (16kHz PCM), on-device Silero Neural VAD (<2.5ms ONNX classification), low-delay Opus compression (24kbps, 20ms frames), and direct private WebRTC/UDP tunneling to a sovereign VPC relay running a streaming Conformer CTC decoder. This delivers a measured glass-to-glass latency of 101.5ms. Local Acoustic Echo Cancellation enables instant verbal barge-in: uttering 'STOP' or 'CROW' dispatches an emergency control datagram (opcode 0xFF) halting LLM generation in <12ms.

answers.question: Why does DevSuperSuite utilize Tree-Sitter AST parsing rather than traditional Vector RAG chunking for code context?
answers.short_answer: Vector RAG splits code across arbitrary token boundaries, breaking type hierarchies and hallucinating interfaces, whereas Tree-Sitter guarantees 100% syntactic and typed contract integrity in <1.2ms.
answers.detailed_response: As documented in ADR-001, Vector RAG relies on statistical semantic proximity, retrieving chunks that 'look' similar while splitting classes and functions mid-definition. This breaks lexical scope, severs type contracts, and induces LLM hallucinations, while adding 200ms–800ms of vector database lookup latency. Tree-Sitter AST slicing constructs exact Concrete and Abstract Syntax Trees in <1.2ms with zero external database dependencies, preserving complete structural contracts and eliminating attention diffusion.

answers.question: How are intermediate source code representations and syntax trees protected in process memory?
answers.short_answer: All intermediate RAM buffers are isolated using POSIX madvise(MADV_DONTDUMP) and zeroized immediately using sodium_memzero() upon tokenization.
answers.detailed_response: To protect intellectual property against cold-boot attacks and operating system core-dump inspection, OmniKernel marks all memory pages allocated for source code parsing with POSIX madvise(MADV_DONTDUMP), preventing the kernel from writing process memory to swap or crash dumps. Immediately following tokenization and payload dispatch, all intermediate AST buffers, parse trees, and audio PCM frames are purged using cryptographic memset (sodium_memzero), ensuring zero plaintext residues.

answers.question: How does the platform isolate autonomous agent tool execution from the host operating system?
answers.short_answer: Agent tools execute within lightweight gVisor (runsc) or Firecracker microVMs with dropped Linux capabilities, read-only root filesystems, and strict seccomp filters.
answers.detailed_response: Autonomous agents given terminal tool execution rights can execute dangerous shell operations. DevSuperSuite isolates all tool executions inside gVisor (runsc) or Firecracker microVMs. Guest Linux syscalls are intercepted in user space, host hardware access is prohibited, execution runs under an unprivileged user (nobody:nogroup), root filesystems are mounted read-only, and cgroup resource limits restrict processes to 512MB RAM and <32 PIDs.

answers.question: How does AgentShield Enterprise detect zero-day unformatted credentials and API keys before commit?
answers.short_answer: AgentShield executes a sub-8ms sliding-window Shannon entropy scan (H > 3.0 to H > 4.5) across staged diffs, catching random cryptographic strings with a 0.2% false-positive rate.
answers.detailed_response: Traditional secret scanners rely on regex matching known prefixes (AKIA for AWS). AgentShield implements mathematical Shannon Entropy H(S) = -Σ p(c_i) log2 p(c_i) evaluated over a multi-scale sliding window (k=32). Natural source code exhibits an entropy of 1.8 to 2.7 bits/char, whereas cryptographically generated secrets (database passwords, HMAC keys, JWT tokens) operate between 3.2 and 5.9 bits/char. Thresholds set at H > 3.0 (with high-entropy tripwires at H > 4.5) intercept 100% of unformatted secrets in <8ms before disk write.

answers.question: How does AgentShield prevent false-positive rejections on package lockfiles, base64 images, and test fixtures?
answers.short_answer: An AST-aware classifier inspects node context, automatically whitelisting known package-lock integrity hashes, compiled assets, and mock fixtures to maintain a 0.2% false-positive rate.
answers.detailed_response: Raw entropy algorithms frequently flag SHA-256 integrity hashes in package-lock.json, compiled SVG data, and test mocks. AgentShield couples entropy calculation with an AST-aware classification function Φ_prune(W_k). If high-entropy tokens are embedded inside recognized lockfile structures, hex color definitions, or designated test fixtures, they are programmatically whitelisted. Ordinary engineering commits pass through in <8ms with an empirical false-positive rate of 0.2%.

answers.question: How does the terminal command proxy intercept dangerous CLI agent commands like 'rm -rf' or unexpected database drops?

answers.detailed_response: Autonomous CLI agents can execute catastrophic shell commands when debugging. AgentShield installs lightweight shell shims wrapping /bin/sh, bash, zsh, and PowerShell. When an agent attempts an operation matching destructive signatures (rm -rf, DROP TABLE, mkfs, kubectl delete namespace), execution is frozen in <2ms. The shim demands a signed administrative one-time token (OTP) or biometric confirmation before execution can proceed, logging the event to SIEM.

answers.question: Why is synchronous pre-commit screening technically superior to asynchronous CI/CD secret scanning (e.g., TruffleHog, GitGuardian)?
answers.short_answer: Synchronous pre-commit blocks secrets in <8ms before disk write, preventing them from traversing local Git history, memory caches, or being ingested by AI agent prompt contexts.
answers.detailed_response: As documented in ADR-002, post-commit scanners (TruffleHog, GitGuardian) execute asynchronously in CI/CD pipelines minutes after code has been committed. During this window, committed credentials reside in local Git history and are actively ingested into autonomous agent memory contexts and cloud prompts. AgentShield attaches synchronously to the local Git pre-commit lifecycle, halting the commit in <8ms before the file touches disk or network buffers.
